transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-03-11 16:00 PT | Duration: 49m | Attendees: Jordan, Priya, Ethan (Redwood); Aisha, Tom, Leah, Carlos (Meridian)

Summary (auto): quick Q1 finops review and reliability deep dive; plan pilot for dedicated capacity for clinical flows.

00:00 Jordan Blake: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'll kick off, this is Jordan from Redwood, with Priya and Ethan on the call. Quick check, everyone can hear me?
00:06 Aisha Rahman: Yep, loud and clear.
00:08 Tom Alvarez: good to go.
00:12 Jordan Blake: Awesome. Agenda — quick usage and cost trend, talk through the two latency incidents last month, then pilot options for dedicated capacity for the clinical scoring path. Priya, want to add?
00:22 Priya Kapoor: Yeah just to add, we'll also go over action items from the last QBR and make sure security questions are up to date.
00:28 Jordan Blake: Cool. Okay, Leah, could you start with a quick run-down on the cost side? I think you had the month-over-month numbers?
00:34 Leah Kim: Sure. So, March so far we're seeing about a 42 percent m-o-m increase in token consumption across our clinical routes, mostly from the new triage model we rolled out mid-February. That bumped our hosted API spend and we're starting to hit the headroom we expected. There's also the embedding batch jobs — those are spiky. We're projecting a 2.6x increase q/q if usage continues.
01:00 Jordan Blake: That's rough but expected with the product launch. Did you break down per-route cost? Where is most of the burn?
01:07 Leah Kim: The top three are the patient-summary generator (about 38 percent), then the triage model (28 percent) and the nightly embeddings jobs (17 percent). The rest is small.
01:17 Ethan Wu: Are you using prefix caching on the summary generator? That route seems like a great candidate.
01:22 Leah Kim: We're not yet. We had tried a naive local cache last month but it wasn't consistent and caused some staleness.
01:28 Ethan Wu: Cool — Redwood has prefix and KV caching options that can reduce tokenization by 40–60 percent in the right patterns. We can run a quick experiment.
01:35 Tom Alvarez: The other thing is latency — we had two incident reports where tail latency spiked above 3.5s for a subset of clinical calls and that caused some downstream timeouts in our UI. Carlos, you pulled the traces?
01:46 Carlos Mendes: Yeah, I pulled the traces. The 03/03 spike lines up with a batch job that started and saturated the burst nodes, autoscaler couldn't spin up fast enough. We also saw higher GC pauses in the workers, maybe model compilation thrash on startup.
02:06 Ethan Wu: That matches what we've seen when models are cold — kernel selection and first few batches can be slow. For that case we usually recommend a small warm pool or pre-warm with a synthetic warm-up traffic during peak ramp.
02:21 Aisha Rahman: How does that work with the hosted plan? We're concerned about cost and also about PII — some of these patient summaries include PHI, we wanted to move them to Dedicated or Private.
02:34 Priya Kapoor: Right, and that's where Dedicated capacity can give you both isolation and more predictable tail latencies because you control the node warm pools. Also we support VPC peering and our Private deployment has full customer-managed control plane.
02:47 Leah Kim: From FinOps perspective, committed capacity could lower unit cost but we need the right sizing to avoid wasted spend. Would love to see scenarios: small committed vs. burst + hosted fallback.
02:59 Jordan Blake: We can model that. Jordan note — prepare committed vs burst scenarios.
03:03 Ethan Wu: For the pilot, we should baseline the current 95/99/99.9 p99 tail. I'll run a continuous 24-hour benchmark with your traffic pattern to measure 95/99/999 latencies and token-cost per route.
03:18 Tom Alvarez: That'd be great. Also, can you include quantized model variants? We experimented with an int8 variant in-house but results were mixed.
03:28 Ethan Wu: Yup — we'll include quantization and a config that shows quality vs token cost. We can run an eval set you provide to check regressions.
03:36 Aisha Rahman: About compliance — SOC2 and audit logs are required for production. We have an upcoming vendor review. What artifacts can Redwood share?
03:45 Priya Kapoor: We have our SOC2 Type II report, audit log exports, and an architecture brief for Private deployments. For KMS, we support customer-managed keys — we can share the technical integration guide.
03:56 Aisha Rahman: Will need the integration doc and the retention settings for logs. Also encryption at rest details.
04:03 Priya Kapoor: Noted. I'll attach the security pack to the follow-up email.
04:07 Leah Kim: On cost optimization, what about batching? Our embedding pipeline is single-threaded and uses very small batches — could larger batching help?
04:16 Ethan Wu: Yes, embeddings benefit a lot from batching and asynchronous workers. We can recommend specific batch sizes depending on average sequence length. For nightly jobs you can schedule larger batches during off-peak.
04:26 Tom Alvarez: The tricky part is the clinical route which needs interactive latencies. We can't batch there aggressively.
04:31 Ethan Wu: Right — for interactive you want prefix caching and smaller model variants or a hybrid fallback to a cheaper model for non-critical steps. Also smart routing by policy can send low-priority requests to cheaper capacity.
04:43 Jordan Blake: We heard earlier that you have fallback logic in your service layer. Would you be open to a canary where non-critical queries go to a quantized cheaper model to save cost and we monitor MRR on error/quality?
04:56 Aisha Rahman: Yes, but only if we can keep a strict validation set and rollback quickly.
05:01 Jordan Blake: Totally. We'll provide a canary plan.
05:04 Carlos Mendes: On the incident root cause, is there a way Redwood can surface autoscaler metrics or provide more fine-grained latency breakdowns per token so we can correlate?
05:14 Ethan Wu: We can provide token-level latency histograms per route and per model, plus an integration hook for trace IDs. That should help correlate with your job scheduler.
05:26 Leah Kim: Also — pricing questions from procurement. They asked about committed credits and step-down clauses — how flexible are the Dedicated contracts?
05:36 Priya Kapoor: We do monthly and annual reserved tiers. For pilots we can do a short-term pilot credit with committed minutes and then negotiate step-downs based on a forecast. Our sales ops can pull a proposal.
05:49 Jordan Blake: I'll include a few contract scenarios in the cost breakdown.
05:53 Tom Alvarez: One more technical ask — do you support on-prem appliance or is Private still cloud-VPC only?
05:59 Priya Kapoor: We have an on-prem packaging option for regulated customers; lead time and support tiers differ but it's available. We'll include the checklist.
06:08 Aisha Rahman: Great. Ok, let's talk timeline for the pilot and benchmarks. Ideally a two-week pilot to validate latency and cost with 24/7 traffic.
06:18 Jordan Blake: Sounds good. Ethan, you'll run the 24-hour benchmark; then we propose a two-week Dedicated pilot with committed small pool and hosted fallback?
06:27 Ethan Wu: Yep that's the plan. For the bench I'll need a replay of your peak hour plus an eval set for quality checks.
06:34 Aisha Rahman: We'll share the replay — Carlos will send traces and sample payloads.
06:39 Carlos Mendes: I'll anonymize PHI, yeah.
06:43 Leah Kim: And we'll share the forecast and procurement timeline.
06:47 Jordan Blake: Great. Any other concerns or blockers?
06:50 Tom Alvarez: Just internal alignment — product and legal need to review the contract but nothing blocking the technical pilot.
06:57 Priya Kapoor: We'll include a checklist for security sign-off to speed that up.
07:02 Jordan Blake: Ok quick recap of decisions: 1) Redwood to run latency tail benchmark 24h; 2) Redwood to model committed vs burst cost scenarios and propose pilot sizing; 3) Meridian to provide replay traffic, eval set, and procurement timeline.
07:18 Aisha Rahman: That matches our notes.
07:21 Jordan Blake: Great. We'll follow up with the security pack and cost scenarios. Thanks everyone.
07:26 End of recording.

Action items (auto): Jordan - cost scenarios; Ethan - bench runs; Priya - security docs; Meridian - traffic/eval shares.

Notes about transcript quality: some product names and acronyms may be slightly off (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K-V cache"), occasional filler words removed for readability.
